items.followUp: Explain how the small intestine absorbs digested food and how the absorbed nutrients are transported.

rubric.why: These are the key substances absorbed from the remaining undigested material.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that the large intestine absorbs water and salts/minerals; award 1 mark if only water or salts/minerals are mentioned.

rubric.why: The remaining material is formed into feces, stored in the rectum and expelled through the anus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing formation or storage of feces and 1 mark for its expulsion through the anus (defecation).

modelAnswer: The large intestine absorbs water and salts from the undigested material.
The remaining material becomes semi-solid feces.
Feces are stored in the rectum.
During defecation, feces are expelled from the body through the anus.

items.followUp: Name four professions or fields in which knowledge of biology is used.

rubric.why: These are examples of careers or fields related to biology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two valid careers associated with biology.

rubric.why: The question asks for four careers; additional valid examples complete the list.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two further valid careers. Do not award this mark for repeating careers already counted.

modelAnswer: Medicine
Agriculture
Fisheries
Forestry

items.followUp: Define a population and distinguish it from a species.

rubric.why: A species consists of a group of organisms of the same kind.
rubric.description: Species as a group of organisms
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a species as a group of organisms of the same kind.

rubric.why: The ability to interbreed and produce fertile offspring is a defining feature of a species.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that members can interbreed and produce fertile offspring.

modelAnswer: A species is a group of organisms of the same kind.
Its members can interbreed with one another and produce fertile offspring.

items.followUp: Name the reproductive organs of a flowering plant.

rubric.why: Roots, stems and leaves are the vegetative organs of a plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least two of the three vegetative organs: roots, stem and leaves.

rubric.why: A complete answer names all three vegetative organs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming roots, stem and leaves.

modelAnswer: The vegetative organs of a plant are roots, stem and leaves.

items.followUp: List the steps of the biological method in the correct order.

rubric.why: Solving a biological problem begins by recognizing it, making observations and proposing a hypothesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the initial steps, including recognition of the problem, observation and hypothesis.

rubric.why: A hypothesis is tested through deductions and experiments, and the results lead to a conclusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming experimentation and the resulting analysis/conclusion steps.

modelAnswer: Recognition of a biological problem
Observation
Formulation of a hypothesis
Deductions from the hypothesis
Experimentation to test the hypothesis
Summarization of results and conclusion
Reporting the results

items.followUp: What substance is obtained from the quina quina tree, and what disease is it used to treat?

rubric.why: Quina quina is associated with quinine, a treatment for malaria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying quinine or its use against malaria.

rubric.why: Without discovery of the tree and its medicinal value, an important treatment for malaria would not have been available.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that malaria patients would lack this treatment or that malaria-related suffering/deaths could increase.

modelAnswer: The quina quina tree provides quinine, which is used to treat malaria.
If the tree had not been discovered, this treatment would not have been available and more people could have suffered or died from malaria.

items.followUp: Write two functions of the nucleus in a cell.

rubric.why: Many cellular metabolic reactions take place in the cytoplasm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cytoplasm is the site of metabolic or chemical reactions.

rubric.why: The cytoplasm holds cell organelles and supports movement of materials within the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the cytoplasm as holding organelles or facilitating transport of materials.

modelAnswer: The cytoplasm is the site of many metabolic reactions in the cell.
It suspends and supports the cell organelles and helps in the movement of materials within the cell.

items.followUp: Define magnification and state how it is calculated.

rubric.why: Resolution describes the ability to distinguish fine detail or two close points as separate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining resolution as the ability to distinguish two close points or fine detail.

rubric.why: Magnification expresses how many times larger the image is than the object.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining magnification as image size divided by object size, or as the number of times an image is enlarged.

modelAnswer: Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate points.
Magnification is the number of times an image is larger than the actual object; it is calculated as image size divided by object size.
